name: CRUCIBLE Ashveil Phantom Stealth Arm
description:
The Ashveil Phantom is a hand-built full arm replacement from Crucible's covert-function line, constructed with signal-dampened servo motors that operate below 18 decibels at all movement speeds — near-silent in ambient environments. The forearm contains three configurable concealed compartments with spring-loaded or pneumatic release, sized to accommodate blades, injectors, data chips, or custom toolsets; compartment linings are Faraday-shielded to defeat active scanner sweeps. The synthetic skin overlay is custom-matched to the buyer's existing complexion and texture, visually indistinguishable from organic tissue at arm's length.

The Ashveil is built to order for a small clientele who value discretion absolutely — intelligence operatives, high-end couriers, fixers who work in rooms where weapons scanners are running. Each unit is unique, hand-assembled by a Crucible artisan over six to eight weeks, and comes with a biometric lock that renders the compartments inoperable if the arm is removed from the registered user. It's expensive enough to be a career investment and discreet enough to justify every credit.
installation_requirements: Full arm amputation or pre-existing amputation; Crucible-approved private surgical installation; custom biometric registration session
rejection_risk: Minimal — Crucible's biocompatible polymer skin layer and hand-fitted socket interface are calibrated per client to minimize any inflammatory response
maintenance: Bi-annual Crucible servicing appointment (house call or secure facility); compartment mechanism lubrication; synthetic skin conditioning treatment

side_effects: Compartment-release reflex conditioning — users occasionally trigger spring-loaded mechanisms during stress responses
Proprioceptive uncanny valley effect during the first month as the brain reconciles the synthetic skin's visual input with the arm's mechanical sensation
Heightened paranoia about scanner detection, even in environments without active scanning
Social discomfort from maintaining the 'organic' performance of the arm in casual settings
cultural_context: The Ashveil exists in a gray space that Meridian 88's legal system treats as a serious offense — the concealed compartments alone classify it as a prohibited concealment device regardless of what's stored inside. Crucible sells through word-of-mouth exclusively, and ownership is an open secret in certain intelligence and fixer circles where the right people simply don't ask each other about their hardware.
known_users: Corporate intelligence operatives and counter-intelligence specialists
High-value couriers transporting sensitive cargo through monitored corridors
Fixers and brokers who work in secured Spire-level environments
Black-market surgeons who carry restricted pharmaceuticals into controlled facilities
Assassins and infiltration specialists operating on long-term embedded assignments
story_hooks: A Crucible Ashveil arm is recovered from an unidentified body — the biometric lock is still active, and whoever cracked the compartments before the party arrived left one item behind deliberately
A Spire-level executive's Ashveil arm has been remotely disabled by someone with access to Crucible's registration system — she's trapped in a negotiation with a concealed weapon she can't reach
Crucible's master artisan who built a specific Ashveil reaches out to the party — the arm's biometric data was copied during installation, and she needs to know who did it before it's sold
